purpose: Aggregate clean-room design patterns learned across the Call of Duty Zombies reference corpus for original HAYUYA/Xziel map generation.

hayuyaRules: change resource availability or pressure state over time
give at least one spoke a shortcut or one-way return

structure: local combat arenas connected by risky corridors
hayuyaRules: at least one door must trade safety for mobility
special enemies must be able to break preferred loops
show destination before committing when possible
provide redundant vertical circulation on larger maps
use light and audio to identify floors
every region must support temporary survival
global landmarking and local route grammar must coexist

structure: same world gains alternate interaction or environment state
hayuyaRules: change mechanics not only color grading

globalRules: A map should have one globally understandable orientation anchor plus regional identity.
Medium and large maps should offer a meaningful early fork and at least one completed loop.
Progression should transform traversal or threat, not only unlock UI systems.
High-round safety must be interruptible by enemy role, hazard, objective, route state or resource pressure.
Spawn pressure is a spatial design problem: entries, sightlines, travel time and concealment matter.
Transport exists to solve scale or verticality and must carry strategic cost or timing.
Power/state changes should alter lighting, audio, machinery and route readability.
Quest primitives should be reusable engine nodes while each map authors original content.
Large-map complexity requires stronger landmarks, shortcuts, local loops and semantic zone identity.
Lighting is part of navigation and threat communication, not a post-process decoration.
cleanRoomGuardrails: No exact reference layouts or room dimensions.
No proprietary assets, scripts, source code, lightmaps, audio, textures or extracted map data.
Use references only for abstract behavior and design principles.
All generated HAYUYA/Xziel content must be original or properly licensed.
